questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> at rest explodes into three pieces, in the ratio of masses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Two smaller pieces fly off perpendicular to each other with velocities of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively. The velocity of the third piece will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Let the masses of the three parts be m', m' and 2m'.

Momentum of first part p1=m'×30=30m' and momentum of second part p2=m'×40=40m'.

Third part will fly in a direction opposite to the direction of resultant of p1 and p2, so that total momentum of the system after explosion remains zero.

Momentum of the third part is p3=p12+p22=30m'2+40m'2=50m'

Velocity of third part, v=50m'2m'=25 m s-1

questions.q: As per the given figure, a small ball P slides down the quadrant of a circle and hits the other ball Q of equal mass which is initially at rest. Neglecting the effect of friction and assume the collision to be elastic, the velocity of ball Q after collision will be : (g = 10 m s-2)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Let vp be the velocity of ball P just before collision. Therefore, applying conservation of energy for P (between the moment it is released and the moment just before collision),

mgl+0=12mvp2

⇒vp=2gl

        =2×10×0.2

         =2 m s-1 

Since both balls have equal masses and the collision is perfectly elastic, the velocities of both the balls will get interchanged.

Therefore, the velocity of ball Q just after the collision is 2 m s-1.

questions.q: A body of mass $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ falls freely from a height of $100 \mathrm{~m}$, on a platform of mass $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ which is mounted on a spring having spring constant $\mathrm{k}=1.25 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$. The bodysticks to the platform and the spring's maximum compression is found to be $x$. Given that $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2},$ the value of $\mathrm{x}$ will be close to :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution: Velocity of $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ block just before it collides with $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ block $=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gh}}=\sqrt{2000} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Using principle of conservation of linear momentum just before and just after collision, we get $1 \times \sqrt{2000}=4 \mathrm{v} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=\frac{\sqrt{2000}}{4} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Initial compression of spring $1.25 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{x}_{0}=30 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}_{0} \approx 0$ using work energy theorem, $\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{g}}+\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{sp}}=\Delta \mathrm{KE}\Rightarrow 40 \times x+\frac{1}{2} \times 1.25 \times 10^{6}\left(0^{2}-x^{2}\right)=0-\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times v^{2}$ solving $x \approx 4 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: The identical spheres each of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>M</mi></math> are placed at the corners of a right angled triangle with mutually perpendicular sides equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> each. Taking point of intersection of these two sides as origin, the magnitude of position vector of the centre of mass of the system is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math>, where the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Position vector r→COM=m1r→1+m2r→2+m3r→3 m1+m2+m3

r→COM =2M×0+2M×4i^+2M×4j^6M

⇒r→=43i^+43j^

|r→|=432+432=423

Therefore, x=3.

questions.q: The momentum of a body is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></math>. The percentage increase in the kinetic energy of the body is_<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mo>%</mo><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The relation of kinetic energy and momentum is given by

K=p22m

The new value of momentum is p'=1.5p

The new value of kinetic energy is

⇒K'=1.5p22m=2.25K

Hence, the percentage increase in kinetic energy is 

K'-KK×100=2.25K-KK=125%
